articles.title: Horse racing live: Newcastle and Newbury’s Coral Gold Cup latest updates
articles.summary: Willie Mullins’s Road To Home one of star attractions. Join the conversation by emailing Greg Wood. Off to Newcastle next for the Rehearsal Chase at 1.25, a three-mile handicap chase that has – in the fairly distant past, admittedly – been a pointer towards the Gold Cup and Grand National.
body: Wendigo, a seven-year-old gelding who races for 4,000 members of the RC Syndicate, was a hugely popular winner of the Coral Gold Cup Handicap Chase at Newbury on Saturday, one of the most prestigious and historic events in the National Hunt calendar.

Sent off favourite at 11-4, Wendigo was not travelling as well as several of his market rivals through the first two miles of the £250k contest. He stayed on best of all in the long home straight, however, and Gavin Sheehan, Wendigo’s jockey, had a three-length lead over the last. Regent’s Stroll, the top weight, ran on strongly up the run-in but was still one-and-a-quarter lengths adrift at the line.

“It’s another dream come true,” Jamie Snowden, the winner’s trainer, said. “It’s one of the most valuable handicap chases outside of the Grand National and to come and win it with a horse that has become the Newbury people’s horse is a dream.

“The further he went, the better he was going and he probably got there a little too soon and idled in front. He’s tough and brave, just like his jockey, and you’re never certain you’ve won until the line comes, but you always thought he would hold on.”

articles.title: Antonelli fastest in Qatar final practice as Mercedes continue domination
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli outpaced Mercedes team-mate George Russell in final practice for the Qatar Grand Prix as the Silver Arrows continued to dominate.
body: Antonelli, who topped both of Friday's practice sessions, outpaced Russell by 0.249s and it looks highly likely a Mercedes driver will be on pole position after qualifying, which takes place later on Saturday at 6pm (build-up from 5.15pm), live on Sky Sports F1.
Mercedes appear to have a half-second advantage over the rest of the field as Max Verstappen was 0.510s adrift of Antonelli and the other Red Bull of Isack Hadjar was 0.687s behind.

Mercedes' dominance is a surprise as nearly every race following August's summer break has been very competitive at the front but it seems a combination of the smooth, high-speed track layout and Mercedes finally getting on top of their upgrades from a month ago has given them a significant margin on their rivals.

"It's looked pretty good so far. We've done it in all the sessions that don't matter, and now we've got to go out and do the job when it counts in qualifying and then tomorrow in the Grand Prix," Mercedes deputy team principal Bradley Lord told Sky Sports F1.

articles.title: Ashley Cole holds talks with Bristol Rovers for first management job in England
articles.summary: Steve Evans on the brink after 3-1 home defeat. Former England full-back last coached Serie B’s Cesena. Ashley Cole is in talks with Bristol Rovers about taking his first management job in England, with Steve Evans on the brink of being sacked.
body: Cole, whose sole senior coaching job was in Serie B with Cesena, is prominent among the candidates to succeed Evans if the League Two club decide to act. The 45-year-old former England and Chelsea defender began his coaching journey at Derby under Frank Lampard, following his former teammate to coach alongside him at Chelsea and Everton. Cole spent time as an assistant to Wayne Rooney at Birmingham. He also had a five-year stint coaching England under-21s as an assistant to Lee Carsley until leaving the post in August in search of his first frontline job in England. Last month League One Bromley interviewed Cole about their vacancy before appointing Karl Robinson.

body: The 28-year-old’s 86th-minute drive from the edge of the area found the net via a bounce and a slight deflection, cancelling out a penalty 12 minutes earlier from Delano Burgzorg.
The substitute converted from the spot after Ben Chrisene had upended Alfie Devine as he tried to latch on to Andrija Vukcevic’s teasing cross.

Norwich had a huge let-off just after the hour mark when Devine ran on to Andrew Moran’s excellent ball over the top before slotting through Daniel Grimshaw’s legs. After a long delay the referee, Tom Reeves, chalked the goal off as he had accidentally touched the ball in the buildup. This contributed to off-field tempers fraying, which ended in the red cards for Clement and Lucketti.

Preston took the lead from the penalty spot in the 74th minute, with Burgzorg squeezing his effort underneath Grimshaw for his first Lilywhites goal. It looked like Graham Alexander’s men were going to hang on until Field drove home the late leveller, connecting well with substitute Jordan Storey’s half-clearance.

articles.title: Great Britain out of Davis Cup as Alcaraz clinches Spain's spot in the final
articles.summary: Leon Smith's near 17-year tenure as Great Britain's Davis Cup captain came to an end with a semi-final defeat to Spain as Cameron Norrie and Arthur Fery suffered straight-sets singles losses to Rafael Jodar and Carlos Alcaraz respectively.
body: Smith, who has been in the role since 2010, was hoping to bow out by leading Britain to a second Davis Cup title under his stewardship, after victory in Belgium in 2015, and an 11th overall.
But it is Spain who will meet hosts Italy in Bologna on Sunday in a rematch of the 2025 final as they aim to stop their opponents from winning a fourth consecutive trophy.

Norrie was overpowered 6-2 7-5 by Jodar before Alcaraz, just under a week out from his ATP Finals success across the country in Turin, routed Fery 6-2 6-1 to extend his personal winning steak to 15 matches, meaning a doubles leg was not required.

Alcaraz raced into a 3-0 lead against this year's Wimbledon semi-finalist Fery and never looked back, with the 23-year-old now looking to add a maiden Davis Cup trophy to a glittering CV that includes the career Grand Slam - he has won seven majors in total - and four titles alone since returning from a wrist injury in August.

articles.title: Work in progress but Liverpool find belief again with Iraola
articles.summary: With the attack finally firing and Liverpool looking more solid at the back, Andoni Iraola has got the fans believing again. Just in time for derby day.
body: A year has passed, and there has been a world of change at Liverpool.
Thursday marked 12 months since the Reds lost 4-1 to PSV Eindhoven at Anfield in the Champions League, the culmination of their worst run of results in more than 70 years.
By the time the final whistle blew that night there were some boos, but Anfield was half empty and belief from the fanbase had evaporated as Liverpool lost for the ninth time in 12 games.

Arne Slot's side had won the Premier League title the season before, but that game against the Dutch side was arguably the nadir of his second campaign in charge. Steven Gerrard said that evening that Liverpool "just keep bleeding".

articles.title: Favourite Wendigo wins Gold Cup thriller at Newbury
articles.summary: Pre-race favourite Wendigo edges past Regent's Stroll in a thrilling sprint finish at Newbury to win the Gold Cup for jockey Gavin Sheehan.
body: Wendigo edged a thrilling sprint finish to win the Coral Gold Cup at Newbury for jockey Gavin Sheehan and trainer Jamie Snowden.
Pre-race favourite Wendigo started slowly, but kept in contention behind the leading group with four fences to go.
It looked to be a tussle for first place between Booster Bob and Regent's Stroll, but Wendigo and Sheehan produced a brilliant finish to charge them down as they approached the final fence.
Regent's Stroll held firm and the horses were neck-and-neck, but Wendigo edged past to win by a length and a quarter, with Booster Bob third.
